texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameFull} is touring the region. Twenty years ago {X_nameDef} was a village healer; now there are songs about {X_objective}, and people walk for days to be seen. {X_nameDef} is in {PLACE} this week and will move on soon.\n\nThey say {X_nameDef} once put back a hand that was gone, and cured a fever no other healer could name. The line outside {X_possessive} door in {PLACE} starts before dawn.

[theirHightech] {X_nameFull}, the surgeon, is touring the region with a van full of equipment and a waiting list longer than the road. {X_nameDef} is in {PLACE} this week and will move on soon.\n\nThey say {X_nameDef} has rebuilt a hand that was gone and cured things other doctors had given up on. Some of that may even be true.

[theirLowtech] Word has come from {PLACE}: {X_nameFull}, the healer, is staying there this week. In the villages they say {X_nameDef} set a broken back once and the man walked home, and that {X_pronoun} can name a fever by the smell of the room.\n\nPeople are walking to {PLACE} from three valleys away. {X_nameDef} won't stay long.

summaries.li: {X_nameDef} could be invited to the colony for a day, to treat {A_nameDef} and teach the colony's own doctor. It costs silver, and the chance won't come again soon.
[invited] {X_nameDef} is on the way to the colony.

texts.li: [!remembered] {X_nameDef}'s assistant has sent word that the healer could stop at the colony on the way to the next town, for {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} has lived with {A_possessive} condition a long time, and {X_nameDef} might be able to do something about it.\n\n{B_nameDef} would give a lot to watch {X_nameDef} work.

[remembered] {X_nameDef} has heard how the colony helped {FACTION} when times were hard, and has sent word: the healer will stop at the colony on the way to the next town, for {COUNT} silver, half what others pay. {A_nameDef} has lived with {A_possessive} condition a long time.\n\n{B_nameDef} would give a lot to watch {X_nameDef} work.

li.label: Invite {X_objective} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The assistant's rider takes the fee back to {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} will come within a few days.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: The colony sends its regrets. {X_nameDef} will be gone from the region soon.

texts.li: [!nothingToMend,taught] {X_nameDef} has come, looked at {A_nameDef} for a long time without saying anything, and asked for hot water and the colony's best light. Now it is done. {ITEM}\n\n{B_nameDef} watched every step and asked a hundred questions, and {X_nameDef} answered most of them.
[!nothingToMend,!taught] {X_nameDef} has come, looked at {A_nameDef} for a long time without saying anything, and asked for hot water and the colony's best light. Now it is done. {ITEM}
[nothingToMend] {X_nameDef} has come and looked {A_nameDef} over carefully, twice, then said there was nothing left that needed a healer's hands. The colony's silver was handed back.
[!nothingToMend] {X_nameDef} has left the colony for the next town, with the colony's silver and its thanks.
[nothingToMend] {X_nameDef} has left the colony for the next town. Whatever ailed {A_nameDef} had mended on its own, and the colony will take that.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef}, the famous healer, came to the colony.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has left the region, and the crowds that followed the healer from town to town have gone home. In the towns they are already arguing over which of the cures really happened.
{X_nameDef} has gone on out of the region, and the line at the healer's door has broken up. The stories about {X_objective} will last longer than some of the cures.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef}, the famous healer, passed through the region.

theirs.li: [their:editors] The sequencers of the Helix Works at {PLACE} have asked {X_nameDef} for a sample, freely given, to learn how one person can mend so much.

theirEnds.li: [their:editors] {X_nameDef} has moved on, and the sequencers at {PLACE} are working through what they learned.

texts.li: Every few years the herds of the region move together, and this is one of those years. The ground shakes at dusk, the birds follow the dust, and the hunters of {FACTION} have come out of {PLACE} in force.\n\nThere will be meat for anyone who wants it, and trouble for anyone who gets in the way.

[fall] The herds are going south ahead of the cold, all of them at once. From the colony the dust can be seen a day before the animals, and {FACTION}'s hunters are already camped along the valleys out of {PLACE}.
[spring] The herds are coming back north with the new grass, so many that the far hills seem to move. The hunters of {FACTION} have come out of {PLACE} to meet them, their winter stores nearly gone.

[theirHightech] The region's herds are on the move, as they are every few years, and {FACTION} have sent their hunters out of {PLACE} with rifles and carts to meet them.\n\nThere will be meat for anyone who wants it, and danger for anyone who gets between the herds and where they are going.

summaries.li: Herds pass the colony far more often, and rare beasts with them. {FACTION}'s hunters may ask to hunt on the colony's land.

texts.li: A party of hunters from {PLACE} has asked to follow the herds across the colony's land. They will keep clear of the fields and the buildings, they say. They would pay {COUNT} silver for the right, or take it as a favor between neighbors.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks they know what they're doing.

Hunters from {PLACE} have followed the herds to the edge of the colony's land, and stopped there to ask. They want leave to cross it and to take what they kill. They'll pay {COUNT} silver, or take it as a neighbor's favor.\n\n{A_nameDef} has had a look at them, and says they know their business.

li.label: Let them hunt
li.outcome: The party thanks the colony and goes after the herds. For days afterward their horns can be heard at dawn.

li.label: Let them hunt, for {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: Their headman pays without arguing, and the party goes after the herds.
li.deed: charged {FACTION}'s hunters to cross its land

li.label: Keep them off the land
li.outcome: The hunters are told to go around the colony's land, and they do.

texts.li: [allowed] The herds have passed, and the hunters of {FACTION} have gone home with full packs. Their horn-blower sounded three long notes as they passed the colony, which among hunters means thanks.
[!allowed] The herds have passed, and the land around the colony is quiet again: trampled in places, greener in others. They'll be back in a few years.
[paid] The herds have passed, and {FACTION}'s hunters have gone home to {PLACE} with full packs. At {PLACE} they say the colony drives a fair bargain for its land.

li.chronicle: The great herds passed through the region.

theirs.li: [their:herders] The herding folk keep their own herd close while the wild herds pass, with riders on its flanks day and night, so that none of it is swept away with them.

theirEnds.li: [their:herders] The wild herds have passed, and the herding folk at {PLACE} have counted their own at dusk. The camp elder says the count came out whole.

texts.li: Something has driven the strange beasts of the far country into the region: animals the old hunters of {FACTION} only know from stories, moving in loose bands and eating anything green.\n\nSome are harmless, and some very much aren't. The hunters of {PLACE} are staying close to home until they know which are which.

[winter] The cold has driven the strange beasts of the far country down out of the high places: animals nobody in {PLACE} has a name for, moving in loose bands through the snow.\n\nOne of them stood at the edge of {PLACE}'s fields all yesterday, watching the houses, and then walked away.

The far country has emptied into the region. Beasts the old hunters of {FACTION} only knew from stories are crossing the hills in loose bands, eating everything green and frightening the herds.\n\nAt {PLACE} they've stopped letting the children out past the fences.

[summer] The heat has driven the strange beasts of the far country out of the high places and into the region's valleys, looking for water. The hunters of {FACTION} have never seen most of them before.\n\nAt {PLACE} they are keeping their own herds penned at night until the beasts move on.

summaries.li: Strange creatures turn up far more often, with herds behind them. A skilled handler may win one over; a careless one may watch it bolt.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} found tracks by the water that don't match anything in the colony's books, and has been out sketching them since.

{A_nameDef} came back from the far fields with a drawing of a footprint as wide as {A_possessive} hand, with four claws where there should be three, and wants to know what kind of animal stands on its toes like that.

titles.li: The hunters of {PLACE} ask for help

texts.li: A rider of {FACTION} came to the gate from {PLACE}. A band of the strange beasts has settled on the town's grazing and will not be moved, and the hunters there would sooner know what they are dealing with before they try.\n\nThey have heard that {A_nameDef} is good with animals, and ask whether {A_pronoun} would ride back with them and look the beasts over for a day or two.

[winter] The strange beasts have come down onto {PLACE}'s winter grazing, and {FACTION}'s hunters have stood watching them across the snow for three days, not knowing which of them will charge.\n\nA rider has come to the colony to ask whether {A_nameDef}, who is said to know animals, would come and tell them.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to {PLACE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has packed for a few days on the road and set off for {PLACE} with the rider.

home.li: {A_nameDef} is back from {PLACE}. {A_pronoun} spent the days at the edge of the town's grazing with {FACTION}'s hunters, watching the strange beasts, and showed them which could be walked off the grass and which were best left alone. {A_nameDef} came home with more to tell about animals than anyone at the colony has heard before.

li.deed: sent {A_nameDef} to look over the strange beasts at {PLACE}

li.label: The colony can't spare anyone
li.outcome: The rider goes back to {PLACE} alone. The hunters there will have to learn about the beasts the hard way.

texts.li: The strange beasts have drifted back toward the far country, or wherever they came from. The hunters of {FACTION} are out again, and the stories about this season are getting bigger by the day.
The strange beasts have gone back into the far country. {FACTION}'s people are out on the hills again, and every one of them has a story about the one that came close.
The strange beasts have left the region, and {PLACE} has let its herds out to graze again. {FACTION}'s hunters are still arguing over which of the beasts could have been tamed.

li.chronicle: The strange herds left the region.

texts.li: The ley lines are restless. Mages in {PLACE} report spells going wrong and spells going far too right, and on clear nights the sky is streaked with colors nobody can name.\n\n{FACTION} have shut their mage towers until it passes. Anyone with the gift will feel it.

[winter] The winter nights have turned strange. The sky over the region burns green and violet after dark, mages in {PLACE} wake up with frost on the inside of their windows, and {FACTION} have shut their mage towers until it passes.\n\nEvery mage in the region is sleeping badly, and dreaming in the same colors.

Mages all over the region woke from the same dream last night, and in {PLACE} the candles burned blue until morning. The ley lines are stirring, and {FACTION} have shut their mage towers until it passes.\n\nAnyone in the colony with the gift has felt it already.

[summer] The short summer nights over the region have turned strange: the sky flickers with color after dark, and the mages of {PLACE} say their spells come out far too strong or not at all. {FACTION} have shut their mage towers until it passes.\n\nAnyone at the colony with the gift will be feeling it too.

summaries.li: Shards fall from the sky more often, and the colony's mages may learn more in these weeks than in a year, if they dare to study the surge.

texts.li: Since the sky turned, {A_nameDef} has hardly slept, and now wants to spend a few nights up with the surge, to see what it can teach.\n\nIt could be a year's study in a week. The mages of {PLACE} say it could also go badly.

{A_nameDef} has drawn the colors of the night sky on every scrap of paper in the colony, and wants a few nights up with the surge, to learn what it has to teach.\n\nThe mages at {PLACE} say it could be a year of study in a week. It could also go very wrong.

li.label: Let {A_objective} study it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sits up nights over the surge, red-eyed and talking too fast, and fills a notebook with diagrams that nobody else can follow.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} comes away from the surge pale and quiet, and won't say what happened. The notebook is full, though.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} stays at the colony, and spends the nights at the window watching the sky.

texts.li: The sky has gone back to its usual colors, and the mages of {PLACE} have opened their towers again. Whatever stirred the ley lines has gone still, and the mages are already arguing about what it was.
The colors have gone out of the night sky, and the shared dreams have stopped. At {PLACE} the mage towers are open again, and every mage in the region has a different account of what happened.
The ley lines are quiet again. The mages of {FACTION} are back in their towers at {PLACE}, and the shards that fell during the surge are being sold in every market in the region.

li.chronicle: A season of wild magic passed.

theirs.li: [their:listeners] The Choir of the Spire at {PLACE} hears the restlessness as a hum gone out of tune, and the cantor has the whole ring singing to hold it steady.

theirEnds.li: [their:listeners] The hum is steady again, the Choir says, and the cantor at {PLACE} has let the ring rest.
